desc: Precompute a cost matrix `cost[j][i]` which represents the minimum increments needed to make `nums[i]` a multiple of `target[j]`.

Use bitmask DP or brute-force over all possible assignments since target length is <= 4. For each target, assign it to one of the nums indices, allowing multiple targets to be assigned to the same nums index.
For each assignment, the cost for target j assigned to nums i is `cost[j][i]`. Sum up costs for all targets.
Return the minimum total cost across all valid assignments.
Implement the solution in the provided method signature.
Implement bitmask DP where `dp[mask]` represents the minimum cost to cover the set of targets in `mask`.
Precompute the cost for each subset of targets and each nums element: for a subset of targets, compute their LCM, then compute the cost to make nums[i] a multiple of that LCM.
Use DP to find the minimum cost to cover all targets (full mask).
Handle edge cases where LCM might be large, but since target values are <= 10^4 and there are at most 4 targets, LCM can be up to ~10^12, which is manageable in Python.
